title: Random forest evaluates two-year risks in a Japanese atrial-fibrillation registry
summary: Random forest models evaluated two-year thromboembolism, major bleeding and mortality risks in 7,406 patients from the J-RHYTHM atrial-fibrillation registry. Thromboembolism discrimination exceeded logistic regression (C-statistic 0.66 versus 0.59), while mortality discrimination was comparable. This retrospective model evaluation used internal cross-validation; participants were Japanese, most received warfarin, and no direct oral anticoagulants were used. Clinical benefits from using the predictions were not tested.

source_review.scope: Primary full article Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata; PMC full article.

evidence.tested: Retrospective 7,406-patient risk evaluation against logistic regression and established scores.
evidence.unknown: External transportability, clinical benefit and performance under current anticoagulant regimens remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: RF with 1,000 trees, training-only feature selection and hyperparameter tuning; 80:20 split and five-fold cross-validation. Prospective registry follow-up does not make this a prospective frozen-model evaluation.
